summary: All 29 assigned features have source/test candidates; no feature is freshly verified or approved by this discovery. Retired workspace/transfer and old all-board inheritance rows require honest stable-ID reconciliation, not reimplementation.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Pinned Node/Worker entry points and local PostgreSQL query/rollback run reproducibly; no cloud account required.
current_acceptance_criteria: Pinned Node and actual local workerd start without cloud credentials; both mount the same product routes.
A fresh disposable PostgreSQL instance proves parameterized query, committed positive control, rollback and safe unavailable DB; close pools/workers.
features.source_behavior: Node binds loopback and injects a four-connection pool; Worker injects a request-scoped one-connection pool, 25-second deadline and environment limits. Local workerd tests exist, not just a Worker-shaped Node function.
unresolved_or_unverified: Fresh local runtime/database checks have not run in this survey. Hosted Hyperdrive behavior is explicitly unverified and is not needed for local harness closure.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Validated request/response schemas and generated OpenAPI agree; fixtures include two projects with distinct members.
current_acceptance_criteria: Request/response schemas and generated OpenAPI describe actual mounted paths, roles, fields, errors, retired routes, OAuth and token restrictions.
Fixtures exercise distinct project memberships, hidden boards and shared-owner context; route inventory parity fails on undocumented/phantom routes.
features.source_behavior: Zod schemas and distinct project fixtures exist. OPENAPI_ROUTES is handwritten descriptive metadata with no request/response schema generation; it advertises obsolete create/transfer and conflicts with live member-directory authority. Existing OpenAPI test only checks version, 30+ route count and logout.
unresolved_or_unverified: Concrete mandatory gap: no generated schema-bearing OpenAPI agreement evidenced; current catalogue is factually stale. Add mounted route/schema parity and current feature fixture coverage.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Clean install and upgrade enforce workspace/project ancestry, versions, uniqueness and receipt/outbox relationships.
current_acceptance_criteria: Clean install plus realistic upgrade to migrations 0001-0020 enforce composite ancestry, versions, uniqueness, receipts and outbox.
Failure rolls migration back; concurrent runners serialize; 0019 runs twice safely and races with personal-workspace creation; embedded Worker migration SQL equals filesystem SQL.
features.source_behavior: PostgreSQL migration runner discovers filesystem migrations or uses embedded SQL, takes an advisory migration lock and commits each migration atomically. 0007 clears board grants on membership status changes; 0019 locks each user during deterministic workspace backfill.
unresolved_or_unverified: Read tests and SQL only; no clean/upgrade database evidence captured now. Require dedicated database per destructive migration suite, embedded SQL parity and final migration-version assertions.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Request IDs, safe errors, deadlines, rate/body limits and structured timing work without exposing secrets.
current_acceptance_criteria: Correlation IDs, safe error bodies/logs, timing, no-store, origin checks, route body bounds and rate bounds cover actual Node and Worker entry points.
Slow/dead request, DB refusal, invalid JSON and limiter failure expose no secrets; side-effect timing after an HTTP deadline is explicitly tested and recoverable through command receipts.
features.source_behavior: Global middleware is mounted. PostgreSQL statement/query timeouts exist. HTTP deadline delegates to Hono timeout; source alone does not establish that underlying DB/provider work is cancelled. Body cap chooses a larger upload allowance by cookie presence, not session validity. System migration catch returns raw error.message.
unresolved_or_unverified: Deadline test covers a slow handler response, not delayed commit cancellation. Test invalid-cookie body caps before calling the large cap authenticated. Assess/sanitize system migration exception details; admin-authenticated scope limits exposure, no external incident established.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Chosen OAuth login creates one identity/session; unsupported callbacks fail closed and private data needs a valid session.
current_acceptance_criteria: Google OAuth state/cookie match and verified provider email precede identity/session issuance; failure issues neither.
One normalized identity and one personal workspace survive concurrent first sign-in; sessions are random bearer secrets stored hashed with secure cookies.
Hosted Worker never exposes email-only dev login; local opt-in requires proper environment/secret.
features.source_behavior: Mounted Google start/callback uses server-side code exchange and verified userinfo email, email upsert, personal-workspace helper, hashed seven-day session, and redirect. Callback failures redirect to fixed sign-in state. Dev login explicitly refuses Worker bindings and requires test mode or deliberate local development configuration.
unresolved_or_unverified: Provider fetches in local tests are synthetic; real signed-in UAT OAuth remains a later integration gate. Re-run Node and workerd negative config/callback cases and concurrency with isolated PostgreSQL.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Logout revokes server session; expired tabs retain safe drafts but cannot keep reading or writing protected data.
current_acceptance_criteria: Logout revokes current hashed server session and clears correctly scoped cookie; repeated/expired logout is safe.
Expired/revoked sessions cannot use reads, writes, private files or cached replays; UI preserves safe unsent drafts and clears protected content when loss is learned.
features.source_behavior: GET session requires auth; middleware fetches nonexpired session per request; logout optionally authenticates then deletes server session and cookie.
unresolved_or_unverified: UI draft/expired-tab behavior and signed-in browser behavior belong to UI/integration evidence; not established by server tests. Clarify logout revokes this browser session; PAT revocation is separate, and PAT UI-session routes must remain denied.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Name/avatar updates display correctly; historical actors remain attributable after grant removal without leaking private account fields.
current_acceptance_criteria: Confirmed first/last names and display-name updates persist; Google refresh does not overwrite chosen name.
Avatar follows an explicitly agreed source; historical actors remain attributable without exposing email/account-private fields.
features.source_behavior: Profile PATCH intentionally accepts display name only and rejects avatarUrl; name PATCH saves both names. Google callback refreshes provider avatar and preserves existing display name. Historical source/tests exist.
unresolved_or_unverified: Catalogue wording name/avatar updates is broader than intentional display-only profile API; resolve whether provider-synced avatar satisfies acceptance. Re-run removed-actor mapping across cards/comments/activity, not just profile success.
features.product_or_architect_input: Architect to record intended avatar behavior from existing accepted scope; if arbitrary avatar editing is required, freeze a new bounded contract before implementation.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Account creates a workspace and exactly one owner atomically; a lost response replay does not create a second workspace.
current_acceptance_criteria: Replace obsolete explicit-workspace creation criteria with personal-workspace ensure on sign-in and POST /projects.
Authenticated old workspace-create route returns typed 410 without writes; anonymous returns 401.
Concurrent ensure and 0019 backfill produce one deterministic primary owned workspace without requiring every invite accept to create one.
features.source_behavior: POST /workspaces is mounted but always retires after authentication. Personal workspace is ensured in Google callback/project creation under user quota advisory lock. 0019 backfills users without workspaces. Old backend handoff still claims workspace POST works.
unresolved_or_unverified: Accepted retirement has source/tests, but TSV/generated checklist/OpenAPI/handoff still describe old behavior; replacement acceptance and fresh review remain required. Do not revive POST workspace to satisfy stale row.
features.product_or_architect_input: Architect must publish amended ACC-04 criteria and retire historical handoff wording; existing accepted decision already authorizes this direction.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owner sets workspace name/timezone; date-only deadlines retain their selected day and shared overdue semantics.
current_acceptance_criteria: Owner alone updates workspace name/timezone with expectedVersion; invalid zone/stale version fails without partial update.
Date-only deadlines keep calendar day and overdue semantics use agreed workspace timezone.
features.source_behavior: Workspace PATCH locks row FOR UPDATE, checks owner and version, then updates name/timezone. It does not require idempotency despite OpenAPI claiming it does. Nonowner existing workspace yields 403, missing workspace 404.
unresolved_or_unverified: Align replay/header documentation with actual version-based update policy. Add date-only/overdue integration checks through preference changes and time-zone/DST boundaries; test fixture timezone alone is not proof. Assess workspace existence response distinction if workspace IDs are meant private.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Show only owned containers and explicitly granted projects; being owner elsewhere grants no extra rights here.
current_acceptance_criteria: Session/project switcher shows only owned containers and explicit project grants; owner elsewhere gains no rights.
Zero-board member still sees project but no hidden board names/counts/default-board IDs.
Shared-only first visit lands /projects; remembered location is reauthorized after revoke/archive.
features.source_behavior: Session derives ownedWorkspaces, accessibleProjects, limits, isOwned and validated lastLocation; project summary uses readable default-board join. Accessible session list is unbounded while primary GET /projects is paginated.
unresolved_or_unverified: Browser context switch clearing and first/remembered landing need UI/integration evidence. Unlimited invited memberships make session payload a later scaling risk; do not falsely call session pagination implemented.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Only current owner transfers to an eligible account atomically; no interval has zero/multiple owners and no stale grant escalates.
current_acceptance_criteria: Ownership transfer stays disabled in beta with authenticated typed 410, unauthenticated 401, and zero owner/version/quota change.
Former-owner boundary tests may use controlled fixture DB changes; these cannot be called successful transfer API evidence.
features.source_behavior: Mounted transfer-ownership route always throws TRANSFER_OWNERSHIP_RETIRED after auth. Accepted later handover explicitly disables beta transfer. Lifecycle test checks retirement then changes owner directly as a controlled fixture. Historical handoff/OpenAPI/TSV claim active transfer.
unresolved_or_unverified: Add explicit anonymous and unrelated authenticated account retirement probes and assert owner/version unchanged. Amend feature/handoff records; do not revive transfer, nor mark old atomic-transfer acceptance fulfilled.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Every endpoint derives active ownership/project grant from session; manager authority is project-scoped and member/viewer cannot administer.
current_acceptance_criteria: Every mounted route and alias enforces active session/PAT route scope, project role and board-grant intersection where board-derived.
Owner implicit access stays within owned workspace; Manager administration is project-only; Member/Viewer cannot grant/change authority.
Manager-created new board grants creator only; only Owner administers others.
features.source_behavior: Shared role helpers resolve owner/project grant; write helper holds workspace/member/grant locks and checks board visibility before role. Board grants are mounted. PAT policy is global before routes, so current acceptance must include both identity modes.
unresolved_or_unverified: Helper/matrix coverage is not inventory coverage. Freeze complete actual route/method/alias matrix and distinguish retired routes; include token expiry/project binding/admin denial after MCP repair. Member-directory role mismatch and status PATCH path require resolution.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Guessing sibling board/card/comment/file/import IDs returns a consistent private not-found response with no metadata leakage.
current_acceptance_criteria: Known-hidden sibling project/board/card/comment/image/upload/import IDs and unknown IDs share agreed private 404 with no private sentinel metadata.
Check actual endpoints, alternate query/body ID selectors, aliases, binary image routes and token project filters, not only verifyProjectAncestry helper.
features.source_behavior: Ancestry helper verifies composite workspace/project relationships. Mounted board-aware read/write helpers protect descendants; full-family access test files exist. Database composite foreign keys backstop ancestry.
unresolved_or_unverified: No mounted family suite executed in this discovery. Re-run all route families against actual PostgreSQL and Node/workerd as claimed; privacy includes response bodies/counts/cursors/errors, not just status.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Grant/owner lock protocol serializes a write against role removal; no write commits after a preceding revocation wins.
current_acceptance_criteria: Two real DB connections prove write-before-revoke and revoke-before-write; no subsequent protected write commits after winning role/grant revocation.
Project/board membership mutations, import commit, image finalization, card/comment writes and replay reauthorization follow one consistent lock order.
features.source_behavior: Project write helper holds FOR SHARE workspace/membership and optional board-grant row; archived context helper locks project/board. Existing forced-interleave suites exercise mounted project update and member-promotion/removal. Full proof still depends on every caller.
unresolved_or_unverified: FLOWBOARD_ACCESS_TEST_DATABASE_URL absence skips important suites; require explicit zero-skip evidence. Status PATCH quota/archive path is outside quota lock protocol; inventory all role/status mutators and test them.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Search, people, assignees, mentions, inbox and historical identity responses expose only the actor's authorized project context.
current_acceptance_criteria: Display identities are project scoped; assignee/mention picker candidates can actually use target board and permitted role.
Historical actors and notifications do not expose account-private fields or hidden board participation; revoked access immediately redacts deep links/content.
features.source_behavior: People route requires boardId for assignees; mentions derive board from active card or explicit board, with empty result when no context. Query helper projects PersonDisplay, filters active grants and eligibility. Separate member-directory endpoint returns email to every active role.
unresolved_or_unverified: Resolve member-directory email/role policy separately from PersonDisplay. Test no-board/foreign-card/removed-actor/user-with-hidden-board cases and inbox after both role and board revocation.
features.product_or_architect_input: Architect/product needs an explicit current directory-role and email-disclosure policy because source/tests permit all active roles while PRJ-05/OpenAPI describe Owner/Manager administration.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Board invitation action explicitly grants project access to all its boards; no hidden board-only permission exception exists.
current_acceptance_criteria: Supersede all-board inheritance with explicit disclosure: project invite grants project only, nonowner needs a board grant, Owner implicitly sees own boards.
Access-summary returns only accessible board counts and no hidden board IDs/counts; invite email cannot promise inherited all-board access.
features.source_behavior: Access-summary mounted under project read lock returns model explicit_board_grants, allBoardsInherit false, hasBoardOnlyExceptions true and visible board count. Historical backend summary and TSV still state opposite inheritance model.
unresolved_or_unverified: Refresh feature definition/handoff prose and invitation disclosure acceptance; source revised payload alone does not approve all affected read/write paths. No new policy decision needed to preserve explicit board grants.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owner creates named projects inside their workspace; each has independent membership and boards.
current_acceptance_criteria: Any signed-in shared-role user can create an owned project through strict POST /projects without choosing/injecting workspace.
New and legacy own-workspace route share 3 active/20 total owned-project caps, actor rate windows, transaction/receipt identity, concurrent serialization and grandfathering.
No membership elsewhere counts toward owned quota; independent boards/memberships and versioned project metadata persist.
features.source_behavior: POST /projects locks user quota, ensures workspace, replays receipt before rate/quota, inserts project and receipt atomically. Legacy own-workspace route remains active. Accepted later handover approves total caps and rates.
unresolved_or_unverified: Update obsolete Owner-only catalogue framing: every user becomes Owner of their own created context, with no increase inside invited project. Re-run concurrent creates/replay through both routes; full feature approval remains open.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owned projects and invited projects are paginated and scoped; hidden projects leak no name, count or existence.
current_acceptance_criteria: Paginated primary project lists include only owned/active granted projects, including zero-board members without hidden board hints.
Invalid/stale cursors and archive filtering are deterministic; defaultBoardId is readable; no sibling name/count/existence leakage.
features.source_behavior: GET /projects delegates to scoped paginated query and PAT project filter. Workspace list uses explicit owner/member locking. Session list is a separate unbounded summary path.
unresolved_or_unverified: Browser Yours/Shared grouping and navigation need UI integration. Test revocation during paginated queries, archived visibility and malformed cursors; do not treat unbounded session payload as paginated.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owner/manager updates project name/description using expected version; managers cannot alter workspace ownership.
current_acceptance_criteria: Owner/own-project Manager updates validated project name/description/brief with expectedVersion and receipt; Member/Viewer forbidden, sibling invisible.
Stale/colliding retries cause no partial metadata/activity writes; archive context blocks edits; ownership/default-board authority remains separately Owner-only.
features.source_behavior: Project PATCH takes actor write-grant lock and writable project lock before replay/update, then saves receipt and commits. Settings adapter owns version/role constraints.
unresolved_or_unverified: Re-run stale replay/revocation races and assert canonical field/activity results. OpenAPI/schema agreement and UI draft conflicts remain separate gates.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owner archives project as read-only and can reopen; data/history remain, trash deadlines continue and new imports/writes stop.
current_acceptance_criteria: Owner-only project archive/reopen retains data/history, blocks domain writes/import/acceptance and does not pause card trash deadlines.
Reopen checks active quota with receipt replay before quota; concurrent create/reopen cannot exceed cap.
Removal/leave must stay available when archived if accepted board decision requires revocation while read-only; role reinstatement must not quietly mutate archived context.
features.source_behavior: Archive/reopen routes exist with Owner lock/receipt; reopen acquires user quota then checks cap. Domain writes call writable-context helper; invitation accept only reads project archived flag without holding project row context lock. Member update normal path omits writable-context check while replay path includes it.
unresolved_or_unverified: Reproduce role/status PATCH in archived project and archive-vs-invite-accept forced interleave. Sequential archived accept refusal does not prove archive race. Verify card restore cutoff continues with actual clock boundaries.
Root-produced baseline JSON was inspected after the source pass: cap bypass and archived-role write are reproduced on this commit; repair and fresh independent review remain open.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owner/manager sees authorized project members; picker exposes only eligible identities and never enumerates unrelated projects.
current_acceptance_criteria: Owner/Manager administrative directory exposes authorized active members; ordinary pickers expose eligible public identity fields within approved project/board context.
No unrelated project membership, email directory or hidden-board participation leaks; removed identities are excluded as new candidates.
features.source_behavior: GET members authorizes active project membership of any role, returns full directory with emails, roles, membership IDs and versions, and nextCursor null. Contract requires email; test deliberately permits Manager/Member/Viewer. This conflicts with administrative OpenAPI minimumRole manager and narrower catalogue wording.
unresolved_or_unverified: Authority/email policy must be reconciled before declaring compliant. Pending decision is not proof source is an exploit: active members may intentionally share a directory, but email access is not explicitly settled by current accepted board decision. Pagination remains absent for administrative members; cap bounds active memberships but grandfathering needs consideration.
features.product_or_architect_input: Record whether Member/Viewer may read administrative member emails. Prefer distinct Owner/Manager administration and email-free public identities unless existing accepted user decision states otherwise.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owner invites manager/member/viewer; project manager invites member/viewer only; invitation names the exact project and inherited boards.
current_acceptance_criteria: Owner invites Manager/Member/Viewer; project Manager invites only Member/Viewer within own project.
Invite establishes project membership only, no implicit board grants; email names exact project without hidden board disclosure.
Name-confirmation, email normalization, 50 seats/pending reservations, rates, transactional activity/outbox/receipt, idempotent replay and duplicate-email race hold.
features.source_behavior: Mounted route takes project quota then write grant/writable locks, checks role and name, replays before rate/caps, creates invite+outbox and schedules mail. No board-grant insertion is in invitation flow. Invitation response includes raw token on initial creation only; receipt minimization is separate.
unresolved_or_unverified: Catalogue inherited-boards clause is stale. Add/locate exact same-email parallel invite test; parallel cap tests alone do not prove duplicate-email behavior. UI invite confirmation/disclosure and real mail adapter delivery remain later evidence.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Durable invite delivery uses a configured email adapter; failure is visible and retryable without logging the secret link.
current_acceptance_criteria: Durable invite outbox survives restart and transient mail failures; configured adapter sends only configured-origin link.
Delivery failure is visible and actionable to an authorized inviter without exposing link/token to logs.
Every terminal state, including retry exhaustion, strips raw token/recipient/template payload; retries are bounded and do not falsely promise exactly-once external mail.
features.source_behavior: Brevo adapter has timeout and outcome classification. Immediate Worker waitUntil send and scheduled outbox drain exist. Invitation list exposes invitation status only, not delivery state. Terminal permanent refusal/delivery sanitize payload, but retry-exhaustion drain branch only sets failed/time/retry_count.
unresolved_or_unverified: Mandatory visible-failure acceptance lacks API outcome exposure in inspected invitation list. Source candidate: exhausted transient retries retain secret payload until 30-day retention, unlike documented terminal sanitization. Test retry-count at max-1, then final retry, then inspect failed payload. No real provider email sent during discovery.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Signed-in verified email must match unexpired, hashed, single-use project token; wrong email grants nothing.
current_acceptance_criteria: Only signed-in verified matching recipient with confirmed name accepts current unexpired hashed single-use token.
Wrong email/expired/revoked/superseded token grants nothing; accepted state, membership, activity and receipt are atomic.
Reaccept/replay after revocation fails; accepted project does not silently gain any board access; caps and archive hold under races.
features.source_behavior: Accept route checks name and token input, locks project quota before invitation; adapter hashes token, FOR UPDATE locks invite, enforces state/expiry/email, supersession timestamp and member cap, then upserts membership. Replay checks active membership; project archive check is unlocked read.
unresolved_or_unverified: Verified email is established by OAuth/authentication chain, not token alone; test dev-login cannot stand for hosted verification. Add archive-vs-accept and replay-vs-removal interleavings; post-accept zero-board UI state needs integration.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Authorized resend rotates token; revoke invalidates it; races create at most one grant and invitation outcome.
current_acceptance_criteria: Authorized resend rotates token and invalidates old pending email; revoke invalidates token; Manager cannot administer Manager invitation.
Resend/revoke/accept races yield one consistent grant/outcome, no deadlock; exact pending/seat caps, expiry rules and replay-before-rate are applied.
features.source_behavior: Resend route locks quota before invitation, validates state/rate/seats; adapter rotates token and supersedes earlier outbox payload. Revoke route and adapter enforce current role and invitation state. Expired resend refusal overrides older helper comment allowing expired invitations.
unresolved_or_unverified: Existing forced accept/resend case is not a complete accept/revoke, resend/revoke and duplicate-resend matrix. Include multiple actual connections, final token/status/grant/outbox invariants and stale replay authority.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owner sees all own projects; manager sees own project invitations; expired/accepted/revoked states and next actions are clear.
current_acceptance_criteria: Owner and own-project Manager list authorized invitations with pending/expired/accepted/revoked state and actionable resend/revoke restrictions; Member/Viewer forbidden, siblings private.
Never return token/token hash; history bounds/pagination and delivery outcomes are accurately documented.
features.source_behavior: Mounted GET takes Manager grant lock then lists project rows with computed expired state; response nextCursor null, query has no LIMIT and includes all historical invitations. Token hash is never selected; delivery outcome not selected.
unresolved_or_unverified: 50 pending cap does not bound accepted/revoked/expired history, so list can grow without bound despite paginated envelope. Need bounded cursor query/schema/UI handoff; delivery-failure field/action tracked with INV-02.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owner appoints/removes managers; manager changes member/viewer roles only and cannot promote self or a peer manager.
current_acceptance_criteria: Owner controls Manager roles; own-project Manager changes Member/Viewer only and cannot modify self/peer Manager/Owner.
ExpectedVersion, replay authority and all status changes preserve project seat cap and pending-seat reservation under concurrency.
Archived project blocks reinstatement/role writes; authorized removal remains possible if revocation exception applies.
features.source_behavior: Member PATCH forwards both role and arbitrary valid active/removed status to updateProjectMember. Adapter locks actor/target and applies authority/OCC, then directly updates role/status. It never takes project quota lock, counts seats or checks archived context on normal path; replay helper checks archive.
unresolved_or_unverified: High source candidate: PATCH a removed Member to active at 50 active bypasses seat cap; concurrent PATCH reactivations can exceed it because only invite/accept use quota lock. Separate candidate: archived role/status write succeeds. Freeze reinstatement policy, reproduce mounted endpoints, then fix at responsible transaction layer.
Root-produced baseline JSON was inspected after the source pass: cap bypass and archived-role write are reproduced on this commit; repair and fresh independent review remain open.
features.product_or_architect_input: Architect chooses whether member-role PATCH may reinstate removed users at all. If retained, it must obey the same quota/archive policy; fresh invite is the simpler existing alternative.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Owner removes any grant; manager removes member/viewer in own project; next API/file/import/replay access fails after revocation.
current_acceptance_criteria: Owner removes any project grant; Manager removes Member/Viewer only; next protected API/file/import/replay is denied.
Removal atomically clears board grants and supersedes/revokes prior invitations; rejoin cannot restore dormant boards.
Both DELETE and PATCH status=removed implement consistent semantics and lock order; removed historical authors remain attributable.
features.source_behavior: DELETE adapter locks target, sets removed, revokes pending project-email invitations and records activity. 0007 trigger clears grants on status change. PATCH status=removed also clears grants via trigger, but omits DELETE pending-invite cleanup and uses different archive/replay handling.
unresolved_or_unverified: PATCH removal is an alternate path requiring parity regression, including stale invitation created before removal. Supersession timestamp fence is counterevidence to automatic old-token escalation; do not call exploit confirmed without reproduction. Test delete and status patch versus held write/replay/import/file delivery.

features.catalogue_acceptance: Invitee can leave their own grant with confirmation; owner cannot leave ownership and historical authorship remains.
current_acceptance_criteria: Active invitee can leave own project; Owner cannot leave ownership; repeated same-key leave returns original safe outcome.
Leaving clears board grants, pending invitations and future API/file access while preserving historical authorship; leave remains possible in archived project per revocation policy.
features.source_behavior: Leave route checks receipt, refuses Owner even on replay, and delegates transactional leave; helper removes membership and revokes pending project-email invites. 0007 clears old board grants. Replay intentionally returns own previous leave success without requiring active membership.
unresolved_or_unverified: Browser confirmation, safe context clearing and historical attribution need UI evidence. Test concurrent leave/accept/reinvite, absent/removed membership, replay after leave and archived-project leave; no test run here.

findings.summary: Handwritten OpenAPI and historical feature/handoff prose contradict mounted retirement and board-access behavior; no schema-bearing generated agreement demonstrated.

findings.classification: confirmed baseline by root-produced mounted PostgreSQL evidence, inspected by survey agent
findings.summary: Member PATCH reinstatement bypasses shared seat-cap lock/count and ordinary role/status changes omit archived-context lock. Root baseline reproduces cap=1 becoming active=2 with HTTP200, and archived role mutation HTTP200 persisted viewer.

findings.classification: mandatory visibility gap plus privacy source candidate
findings.summary: Invitation delivery failure is internal only; exhausted transient retries mark failed without clearing token/recipient/template payload.

findings.classification: policy mismatch; do not call confirmed authority exploit
findings.summary: Member/Viewer can read administrative member directory with emails, roles and membership IDs despite narrower catalogue/OpenAPI authority.
Invitation list is unbounded across historical outcomes; 50-pending cap does not cap history.
Invitation accept reads project archive state without holding writable-project row lock; sequential archive denial does not prove concurrent archive serialization.
PATCH status removal omits DELETE pending-invitation cleanup; timestamp supersession fence is relevant counterevidence to automatic rejoin exploit.

actions: At active-seat cap, PATCH removed member to active; force two parallel reactivations; assert active+pending invariant under accept/reactivate.
Archive project then PATCH role/status; force archive-vs-accept to assert one serialization order. Test DELETE and PATCH removal plus old invitations and board grants.

actions: Unify permitted membership-state changes at quota/archive/authority transaction layer; preserve removal while archived when allowed and use consistent replay checks.

Implement authoritative request/response OpenAPI generation or a complete validated spec plus actual route parity; accurately describe retired endpoints, name/profile, project creation and token restrictions.

actions: Provision only new local disposable PostgreSQL instances; inspect local target guard before tests; never reuse hosted URL. Run relevant focused suites then complete API/contracts/typecheck/build with all access suites enabled.
